summary: 董卓废辩而立，九岁即位；迁都长安、东归洛阳、都许，禅位于曹丕，汉亡；逊位为山阳公十四年。
summary_en: Raised by Dong Zhuo in place of Bian, enthroned at nine; he moved to Chang'an, wandered east, settled at Xu, and abdicated to Cao Pi, ending the Han; he lived fourteen years as Duke of Shanyang.

bio_md:
# 汉献帝 · 主要事迹

刘协是[[e-han-ling|灵帝]]次子。中平六年，董卓废[[e-han-shao-bian|少帝辩]]，立年九岁的刘协，是为献帝——汉家四百年天下的最后一位皇帝，从此开始了他作为「流动的玉玺」的三十一年。

初平元年，董卓逼迁长安，焚洛阳宫室，东汉中枢第一次流离失所；初平三年，王允与吕布诛董卓，旋为李傕、郭汜所败，长安再乱。兴平二年，献帝出长安东归，一路为乱兵所劫，食枣栗度日，流离曹阳、弘农之间。建安元年，曹操迎帝都许，「奉天子以令不臣」——献帝终于有了一个固定的都城，也终于有了一个不可摆脱的主人。

都许之后的二十四年，是曹操父子经营天下的二十四年，也是献帝作为禅让道具的二十四年：建安五年官渡之战、十三年赤壁之战，皆在许都的名义下进行；建安十九年，曹操杀伏皇后，献帝只能默然；二十五年（延康元年），曹丕受禅，献帝逊位，封山阳公，东汉正式灭亡。他做了三十一年皇帝，从未有过一天的实权，却以「建安」年号为名，见证了整个三国格局的形成。

逊位后的献帝在山阳做了十四年公，于魏明帝青龙二年薨，年五十四，以汉天子礼葬。史评「得位屯蹇，版荡云海」，正是他一生最贴切的注脚：汉祚四百年，始于[[e-han-guangwu|光武]]之中兴，终于献帝之禅代。

> 参考：点校本《后汉书》卷009《孝献帝纪》、《董卓传》，《三国志》武帝纪、文帝纪，谭图第 2 册。

bio_parts_en.value: Liu Xie was the second son of
. In the sixth Zhongping year, Dong Zhuo deposed

and raised the nine-year-old Xie as Emperor Xian — the last emperor of the four-hundred-year Han, beginning his thirty-one years as a "movable imperial seal."

In the first Chuping year Dong Zhuo forced the court to Chang'an, burning the palaces of Luoyang: the Eastern Han center was uprooted for the first time. In the third Chuping year Wang Yun and Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo, only to be overthrown by Li Jue and Guo Si; Chang'an fell into chaos again. In the second Xingping year the emperor left Chang'an and fled east, robbed by the soldiery on the road, living on dates and chestnuts, drifting through Caoyang and Hongnong. In the first Jian'an year Cao Cao received the emperor and settled the court at Xu — "supporting the Son of Heaven to command the disobedient." Xian at last had a fixed capital, and at last a master he could never shake.

The twenty-four years at Xu were the years of the Cao house's conquest of the realm, and of Xian's role as the prop of an abdication: the Guandu campaign of Jian'an 5 and the Red Cliffs of Jian'an 13 were fought under his name; in Jian'an 19 Cao Cao slew Empress Fu, and Xian could only be silent; in the first Yankang year (220) Cao Pi received the abdication, and Xian was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang. Eastern Han was formally finished. He had been emperor for thirty-one years without a single day of real power, yet under his "Jian'an" era name the whole Three Kingdoms pattern took shape.

As Duke of Shanyang he lived another fourteen years, dying in the second Qinglong year of Wei at fifty-four, buried with the rites of a Han emperor. The historians' verdict — "he got the throne in hardship and drifting, tossed on the waves of the age" — fits him exactly: the Han mandate, opened by

's restoration, closed with Xian's abdication.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Hou Hanshu*, ch. 9 (Benji of Emperor Xian) and the biography of Dong Zhuo; the *Sanguozhi*, biographies of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao) and Emperor Wen (Cao Pi); Tan Qixiang's atlas, vol. 2.
